title: Robot Vision
tagline: Give a robot a camera, and teach it to find and follow things.
description: Give a robot eyes: camera basics, colour and shape detection, tracking, and guiding an arm to what it sees.
outcome: After this course you can explain how a robot finds an object in a picture and guides an arm to it.
whoFor: Learners who want a robot that can see, find and follow objects.
outcomes: Explain a picture as a grid of numbers
Find an object by colour and shape
Work out where an object is
Guide an arm to a seen object, and teach a robot to recognise things

finalActivity.title: Show-day checklist
finalActivity.prompt: Write a show-day checklist for your robot: what you will test before the public sees it, how you will deal with glare, and how it stops safely.

lessons.title: A camera is a grid of numbers
lessons.summary: Explain that a picture is made of pixels with numbers.

quiz.q: What is a pixel?
options: One tiny dot of a picture
quiz.why: A picture is made of many tiny dots called pixels.

quiz.q: To a robot, a picture is…
quiz.why: Each pixel is stored as numbers.

quiz.q: A bigger number in a brightness picture usually means…
quiz.why: Larger values are brighter.

quiz.q: A colour picture uses several numbers per pixel because…
options: Colour is built from red, green and blue amounts
quiz.why: Mixing red, green and blue makes colours.

lessons.title: Finding colour
lessons.summary: Find an orange cup using a colour rule and a mask.

quiz.q: What is a colour rule?
options: A test that checks whether a pixel is in a chosen colour range
quiz.why: The rule says which pixels count as the target colour.

quiz.q: A mask shows…
quiz.why: A mask marks matching pixels.

quiz.q: Why use a range of colours instead of one exact value?
options: Lighting changes the exact colour you see
quiz.why: Real objects look slightly different in different light.

quiz.q: If the mask shows the cup as a white blob, then…
options: The robot has found where the colour is
quiz.why: The blob marks the matching area.

lessons.title: Where is it?
lessons.summary: Work out an object position and rough distance from a picture.

quiz.q: How can you find an object's position in the picture?
options: Find the centre of its blob
quiz.why: The centre of the blob gives its position.

quiz.q: A cup that looks bigger in the picture is usually…
quiz.why: Nearer objects appear larger.

quiz.q: If the blob is left of centre, the robot should…
quiz.why: Turn toward the object to centre it.

quiz.q: Why is distance from a picture only rough?
options: Size depends on the real object and the lens
quiz.why: You must know how big the object really is to be accurate.

lessons.title: Light and noise
lessons.summary: Handle changing light and speckles in a picture.

quiz.q: What is 'noise' in a picture?
options: Random speckles that are not real objects
quiz.why: Noise is stray pixels that confuse detection.

quiz.q: A simple way to remove tiny speckles is to…
options: Ignore blobs that are too small
quiz.why: Filtering by size removes specks.

quiz.q: Changing light can make a colour rule fail because…
options: The same object looks different in different light
Light is a kind of noise in motors
quiz.why: Brightness and tint change pixel values.

quiz.q: To cope with changing light you can…
options: Widen the range or add steady lighting
quiz.why: Better lighting or a wider range helps.

lessons.title: Edges and shapes
lessons.summary: Tell similar objects apart by their edges and shape.

quiz.q: An edge in a picture is…
options: A sudden change from dark to light
quiz.why: Edges are where brightness changes sharply.

quiz.q: Why use shape as well as colour?
options: Two objects can share a colour but differ in shape
quiz.why: Shape separates look-alikes.

quiz.q: A round cup and a square box can be told apart by…
quiz.why: The outline differs.

quiz.q: Counting corners of an outline can help to…
quiz.why: Corner counts describe shapes.

lessons.title: From camera to arm
lessons.summary: Turn a position in the picture into a position on the table.

quiz.q: Why can't the arm use picture positions directly?
options: The arm works in table positions, not pixels
quiz.why: Pixel positions must be converted to table positions.

quiz.q: A simple way to link them is to…
options: Mark known spots and match them to picture positions
quiz.why: Matching known spots builds the link.

quiz.q: If the camera moves after calibration, you should…
quiz.why: A moved camera breaks the link.

quiz.q: A good test is to…
options: Ask the arm to touch a spot the camera found
quiz.why: Touching the found spot checks the link.

lessons.title: Tracking a moving object
lessons.summary: Follow something that moves with look, compare, correct.

quiz.q: The tracking loop is…
quiz.why: The robot repeatedly looks and corrects.

quiz.q: If the object moves right, the robot should…
options: Turn right to keep it centred
quiz.why: Turn to follow it.

quiz.q: Why track many times per second?
quiz.why: Fast updates keep up with motion.

quiz.q: If the robot loses the object, a good plan is to…
quiz.why: A safe search is better than guessing.

lessons.title: Learning to recognise
lessons.summary: Teach a robot to name objects from examples.

quiz.q: How do you teach a robot to recognise a cup?
quiz.why: Learning uses many labelled examples.

quiz.q: Why show examples in different light and angles?
options: So it works in real situations
quiz.why: Variety makes recognition robust.

quiz.q: If the robot names a cup 'bottle', it needs…
quiz.why: More varied examples fix mistakes.

quiz.q: Recognising is different from colour finding because…
options: It can tell what the object is, not just its colour
quiz.why: Recognition understands the type of object.

lessons.title: See, decide, grab
lessons.summary: Join seeing, deciding and acting into one loop.

quiz.q: The full loop for picking up a cup is…
quiz.why: Seeing leads to a decision and then an action.

quiz.q: If the cup is not found, the robot should…
options: Not move the arm and look again
quiz.why: Don't act without a target.

quiz.q: Checking after the grab helps to…
options: Confirm the cup was really picked up
quiz.why: Verification catches missed grabs.

quiz.q: Combining parts works best when you…
options: Test each part first, then together
quiz.why: Testing in stages finds problems early.

lessons.title: The big fair
lessons.summary: Prepare a robot for a real crowd, glare and surprises.

quiz.q: Why make a checklist before a show?
options: It stops you forgetting important checks
quiz.why: Checklists catch forgotten steps.

quiz.q: Glare from bright lights can…
quiz.why: Glare washes out the picture.

quiz.q: A safe stop is important because…
quiz.why: A safe stop limits harm around people.

quiz.q: Before the fair you should…
options: Practise in similar light and crowds
quiz.why: Rehearse in conditions like the real event.
